title: Quadrilles, waltzes and ball suppers
summary: Description of the quadrille, why it was dropped, ball suppers, and the dances of her youth.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: You know what they cut out... And look, they used to play long tunes. It wasn't like y'all now. And they cut out all them quadrilles. They had quadrilles and large ones. And getting ready to have that quadrille. That was fun. Because if a man knew how to dance, he showed himself then. And when they'd holler, they'd holler almost like the chicken. And they'd holler, swing your partner. Swing your partner. Swing your partner. Swing your partner. They'd holler, swing your partner. And you know how they do for the quadrilles. And they'd holler, grab your partner. And the man would grab the lady and swing out. Then they'd say, swing your partner. And the man would come and cut out his steps all in front. You know the lady. And she'd be making her motions too. And that was good. And they'd hand their hand. And they'd say, chain. Chain something. Some boy. And they had the ladies and men. Everybody catch their hands together. And they'd be going, oh, that was really grand. You know why they cut it out? Your daddy said, because it was so long, the people would give the ball. After they realized a number of years after that, they was losing money. Because them days, people would give balls. And every time bands stopped playing, well, the gentlemen would take the lady to get refreshment or supper. And when I was going to the ball, it wasn't like y'all heard about. I don't have nothing to eat. We had turkey, ham, and gumbo, and all that. 40 cents for a nice turkey dinner. The young ladies didn't drink no beer. It would be a disgrace if somebody would go tell your parents to see you getting a beer in the ball. Ladies didn't go around. You know, not no young ladies. Maybe the elder women would go up in there. And you had very few to do that. But more so, the pops, you'd have pop. And I wouldn't say it was punch. It was lemonade, you know. But you would really get that something to eat, though. They'd treat you to that. And when they'd have the... Some of the gals would hardly... I just loved to dance so much, I didn't care about nothing to eat. I mean, we'd take a pop. But if the band would... And they'd strike up, hit the foot, and then ta-ta, ta-ta. And then when the band would get ready to strike, you'd see everybody, if they're going to have the quartile, they'd blow the horn, you know, to give you the... See if they're going to have the quartile. And you'd be looking for your party, you know, who could dance that, you know.
What kind of tune was that play, ma?

Like what? I just can't think of it now, see. But... I saw my names, you know. Yeah, Dad, I mean Uncle Arthur and Cousin Walt and Bob, and he was a handsome-looking fellow. And they had very small... You know, and they could make all the motions, and I mean, they're making that step. The numbers used to be real fast.

For the quartile? Yeah. Certain times, depending what, you know, certain things. But the walls, when you had to walk, you know, it wasn't. Not all of them was fast. And they had, they had, they played a mazooka. They had a waltz, and they had shatters. They all don't play that. They all don't have no shatters. You know how the shatters was. They make so many steps, and the ladies put this out a little bit, and the man waltz around. The shatters was beautiful. They have it, what you call them? Murray, Murray has them shatters and everything. Arthur Murray can dance them. Arthur Murray can dance them shatters. I mean to tell you, he really dances them waltzes and everything. That man can dance. And you see them shatters on there, alright. They're still doing it some places. Cousin Leona does that. Cousin Leona.
Oh yeah, she still does that. Every year. Oh yeah, she still does that.
